heading: Tree depth = 1 + deeper child
body:
Maximum depth of a tree rooted at any node equals **1 (the current node) + the maximum depth of its deeper subtree**.

This recursive insight means each node asks its children for their depths, picks the larger, adds 1, and returns it upward.

Base case: empty tree (`None`) has depth 0.

heading: When to use this pattern
body:
Use **recursive DFS** when:
- You need tree height or depth
- The answer at each node depends on combining child answers
- Problem has natural base case (leaf/null)

Common mistakes:
- Forgetting base case (`None` → 0)
- Off-by-one errors (forgetting to add 1 for current node)

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
options: O(h) where h is the height
explain: We must visit every node exactly once to compute the maximum depth, making the time complexity O(n).
